summary: Cut at 6.5, the same score as round 2. This is round 3, and the ring is still below the 7.5 ship bar and the Caiman finish bar of 7. The read is still strong: at 300 px it is a blue oval between two fanned three-feather wings. The lesson is better than in round 2. Feature 9 now declares the Tier extrudes 6 to 8 as its sources (consumes/reads [6,7,8]), and its three tips in frame 10 land where the slab tips sit in frame 9. But it is still a baked Stored mesh with its own spine numbers in the recipe, so the sketch does not really drive the finished wing. The craft punch list from round 2 is mostly still open. The bullet-shaped clasp nubs beside the collet are still there, now with small spurs (side.png, reverse.png, shoulder.png). The primary tips have been narrowed from about 1.6 mm to 1.0 mm, but they now end in a stepped collar and capsule cap, which reads as a nozzle or a fingertip in shoulder.png and hero.png. The tip is not a point. The jagged star is still in the collet seat in palm.png. The collet is still a plain straight tube, and frame 4 'Collet foot' still adds nothing you can see. The gates also regressed. Each wing part now records census_below_floor_off_lip 10 in the draft and 7 in the export, with samples down to 0.010 mm at theta 44 to 53 that are neither lip nor tip. In round 2 this was 0. The report's gate line still claims a pass. The collet lip also samples 0.39 mm at theta 90, which is under the 0.5 mm lost-wax minimum section.
strengths: It reads straight away at 300 px with no caption: a winged oval sapphire. face-300 is symmetric, and hero-300 shows three separate tips on the near wing.
The barbed feather texture and the fanned headings (45/22/0) make a recognisable jewellery motif, and the shank is plain to the palm as the section asks.
The timeline now ties the sculpt to the sketch on paper. Feature 9 lists Tier I to III as its sources, and the frame-10 tips line up with the frame-9 slab tips to within about the 0.5 mm asked.
The silhouette is distinct from every starter and from the other Officina lessons.
Geometry gates are green on draft and export: watertight, 1 shell, 0 degenerate faces, 0 crossings, all 11 features Ok, field verdict Castable, 0 DFM findings, and 1,290,118 export triangles.

checklist.item: Finished piece, not a CAD demo (proportion, weight, meeting with the band)
checklist.reason: The clasp-feather roots still end in bolt-like knobs at about theta 78 and 102, now with spurs (side.png, reverse.png). The collet is a plain straight cylinder with a dark shelf at its base in side.png, with no visible foot or seam bead. In side.png the wings run as straight planks, with a dark gap under them near the collet.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD
checklist.reason: Every primary ends in a stepped collar and capsule cap: a turned, mechanical termination, not a feather point (shoulder.png, hero.png, the upper-left tips in face.png). w_tip 1.0 mm missed the 0.6 mm asked. The clasp still has w_tip 1.4 and tip resolution 12.

checklist.item: Outlines crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: palm.png still shows the jagged star in the collet seat. face.png shows faceted cap planes at the outer tips. The barbs smear into streaks where the primaries converge on the collet.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings and visible
checklist.reason: The oval 7 x 5 sits in a head.bezel collet and is clearly visible in the face, hero and stones views. 1 stone previewed and 1 reported.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable: the band is a procedural DShape ReverseTaper.

Frames 5 to 10 now follow on: plane, sketch, three tiers, then a sculpt whose tips match the tiers. But frame 4 'Collet foot' is still identical to frame 3 (a Stored mesh with no visible change), and feature 9 is still a baked Stored mesh. A student cannot see how the slabs became barbed feathers.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from the other Officina rings and the starters
checklist.reason: A swept wing pair round a north-south oval. Nothing in the starters or the other lessons looks like it.
